nodes.summary: Along a solution of a mass-action system with positive rate constants and a positive complex-balanced equilibrium `c*`, positive and differentiable (two-sided) at every `t ≥ 0`, `G(x t)` is nonincreasing on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: The pseudo-Helmholtz function does not increase along solutions

nodes.summary: The complexes of the network: the sources and products of its reactions.
nodes.title: Complexes of a chemical reaction network

nodes.summary: The deficiency `δ = n - ℓ - s` (number of complexes, linkage classes, dimension of the stoichiometric subspace).
nodes.title: Deficiency of a chemical reaction network

nodes.summary: Two positive vectors whose difference lies in a subspace `W` and whose logarithms differ by a vector orthogonal to `W` are equal.
nodes.title: Birch's theorem, uniqueness

nodes.summary: A weakly reversible mass-action network of deficiency zero has, for any positive rate constants, a positive complex-balanced equilibrium. Together with `existsUnique_equilibrium_of_isComplexBalanced` this gives `existsUnique_equilibrium`.
nodes.title: Horn–Feinberg: complex balancing for every choice of rate constants

nodes.summary: For any subspace `W` of `S → ℝ` and positive `a`, `b` there is a positive `c` with `c - b ∈ W` and `log c - log a` orthogonal to `W` (for the dot product). Source: Birch (1963); Horn & Jackson (1972).
nodes.title: Birch's theorem, existence

nodes.summary: If a mass-action system with positive rate constants has a positive complex-balanced equilibrium, then each positive stoichiometric compatibility class `(x₀ + 𝒮) ∩ ℝ_{>0}^S`, `x₀ > 0`, contains exactly one positive equilibrium. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972); Feinberg (2019), ch. 15.
nodes.title: Horn–Jackson: one equilibrium per compatibility class

nodes.summary: A weakly reversible mass-action network of deficiency zero has, for any positive rate constants, exactly one equilibrium in each positive stoichiometric compatibility class.
nodes.title: Deficiency-zero theorem, weakly reversible case

nodes.summary: The pseudo-Helmholtz function has time derivative `helmholtzRate` along a solution of the mass-action system, at any time where the solution is positive.
nodes.title: Pseudo-Helmholtz function along positive mass-action solutions

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `helmholtzRate_nonpos`, the rate of change of the pseudo-Helmholtz function vanishes at a positive `c` exactly when `c` is an equilibrium. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972).
nodes.title: Equality in the Horn–Jackson inequality

nodes.summary: If `c*` is a positive complex-balanced equilibrium for positive rate constants, the pseudo-Helmholtz function does not increase along the mass-action vector field at any positive `c`. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972); Feinberg (2019), ch. 15.
nodes.title: Horn–Jackson inequality

nodes.summary: The rate of change of the pseudo-Helmholtz function along the mass-action vector field, `∑_s (log c_s - log c*_s) f_s(c)`: the derivative of `pseudoHelmholtz cstar` at `c > 0` applied to `massActionField k c` (`hasDerivAt_pseudoHelmholtz`).
nodes.title: Rate of change of the pseudo-Helmholtz function

nodes.summary: If a mass-action system with positive rate constants has a positive complex-balanced equilibrium, then every positive equilibrium is complex balanced.
nodes.title: Horn–Jackson

nodes.summary: Concentrations `c` are complex balanced for the rate constants `k`: at every complex `z`, the total rate of the reactions with source `z` equals the total rate of the reactions with product `z`. (Complexes that occur in no reaction give `0 = 0`.)
nodes.title: Complex-balanced concentrations

nodes.summary: The network is weakly reversible: for every reaction `y → y'` there is a directed path of reactions from `y'` back to `y`.
nodes.title: Weakly reversible reaction network

nodes.summary: The undirected reaction graph on the complexes: distinct complexes are adjacent when one reacts to the other.
nodes.title: Linkage graph of a reaction network

nodes.summary: A complex-balanced state is an equilibrium of the mass-action system (for all real `c` and `k`). Source: Horn & Jackson (1972).
nodes.title: Complex-balanced states are equilibria

nodes.summary: The mass-action vector field with rate constants `k`: `x ↦ ∑_r k r (∏_s x_s ^ (src r s)) (prod r - src r)`.
nodes.title: Mass-action vector field

nodes.summary: A mass-action network of deficiency zero that is not weakly reversible has no positive equilibrium for any positive rate constants.
nodes.title: Deficiency-zero theorem, non-weakly-reversible case

nodes.summary: The number of linkage classes: connected components of the undirected reaction graph.
nodes.title: Number of linkage classes of a reaction network

nodes.summary: If `c*` is a positive complex-balanced equilibrium for positive rate constants, the positive equilibria are exactly the positive `c` whose `log c - log c*` is orthogonal (for the dot product) to the stoichiometric subspace. Source: Horn & Jackson (1972); Feinberg (2019), ch. 15.
nodes.title: Horn–Jackson: the positive equilibria

nodes.summary: The pseudo-Helmholtz function `G(c) = ∑_s c_s (log c_s - log c*_s - 1)` relative to the reference concentrations `cstar` (Horn & Jackson 1972). It is meaningful for positive `c` and `cstar`; elsewhere `Real.log` takes junk values.
nodes.title: Pseudo-Helmholtz function

nodes.summary: The mass-action rate `k r * ∏_s c_s ^ (src r s)` of reaction `r` at concentrations `c`.
nodes.title: Mass-action reaction rate

nodes.summary: A chemical reaction network on the species `S` with reactions indexed by `ρ`: reaction `r` turns the source complex `src r` into the product complex `prod r` (stoichiometric coefficients).
nodes.title: Chemical reaction network

nodes.summary: The directed reaction relation on complexes: `y ⟶ y'` if some reaction has source `y` and product `y'`.
nodes.title: Directed reaction relation on complexes

nodes.summary: The stoichiometric subspace: the span of the reaction vectors `prod r - src r`.
nodes.title: Stoichiometric subspace

nodes.summary: Complex balance at `c` rewrites the rate-weighted sum of any function of the products as the same sum over the sources (for all real `c` and `k`).
nodes.title: Complex balance exchanges source and product sums
